references.text: Abraham's faith when he was tested: He offered Isaac as a sacrifice, believing that God could raise him from the dead.
James writes that Abraham was justified by works when he placed his son Isaac on the altar – faith worked together with his actions.
The angel's intervention that stopped Abraham from slaughtering Isaac, and the ram that was sacrificed in his place.
Paul draws a parallel: God did not spare His own Son – a typological connection to Abraham, who was willing to offer his son.
The suffering servant is led away like a lamb to slaughter – a prophetic parallel to Isaac's sacrifice.
The preceding dialogue between Abraham and Isaac about the sacrificial animal, which shows Abraham's faith: 'God will provide for Himself the lamb.'
The verses illuminate each other by showing the connection between Abraham's inner grief (21:11) and his outward act of total obedience (22:10) in the test with Isaac.
